q: A nuclear reaction is a process in which a particle or a gamma radiation penetrate into a nucleus and changes its configuration.
e: True. A nuclear reaction is a particle or gamma entering a nucleus and rearranging it. Or a gamma radiation penetrate into a nucleus and changes its configuration.

q: If the total mass before a nuclear reaction takes place is greater than the total mass after reaction, this mass defect is absorbed as energy.
e: False. The right claim is this: If the total mass before a nuclear reaction takes place is greater than the total mass after reaction, this mass defect is released as energy and this type of reaction is known as exothermic reaction. Exothermic nuclear reactions lose mass; that mass defect leaves as energy. The printed line wrongly says if the total mass before a nuclear reaction takes place is greater than the total mass after reaction, this mass defect is absorbed as energy.

q: An endothermic nuclear reaction requires external energy to be provided for the reaction to take place.
e: True. Endothermic nuclear reactions need extra energy because the products are heavier. Requires external energy to be provided for the reaction to take place.

q: When a neutron strikes and penetrates a nucleus of uranium-235, the nucleus becomes highly unstable and splits into two lighter nuclei.
e: True. Nuclear changes happen in the nucleus, not in the electron cloud of chemistry. Uranium-235, the nucleus becomes highly unstable and splits into two lighter nuclei.

q: The splitting process of a nucleus is called fusion.
e: False. The right claim is this: When a neutron strikes and penetrates a nucleus of uranium-235, the nucleus becomes highly unstable and splits into two lighter nuclei, shooting out two or three neutrons; this splitting process is called fission. Fission splits a heavy nucleus after a neutron bite, throwing fragments and more neutrons. The printed line wrongly says the splitting process of a nucleus is called fusion.

q: For a chain reaction to be maintained, the uranium-235 has to be below a certain critical mass.
e: False. The right claim is this: For a chain reaction to be maintained, the uranium-235 has to be above a certain critical mass. A chain reaction is when fission neutrons go on to split further fuel nuclei. The printed line wrongly says for a chain reaction to be maintained, the uranium-235 has to be below a certain critical mass.

q: The energy released per atom in a nuclear reaction is about a million times greater than the energy released per atom from a chemical reaction.
e: True. A nuclear reaction is a particle or gamma entering a nucleus and rearranging it. Times greater than the energy released per atom from a chemical reaction.

q: A nuclear reactor is a device in which a fission chain reaction can be initiated, maintained and controlled.
e: True. A reactor is a vessel where a fission chain can be started, held, and steered. In which a fission chain reaction can be initiated, maintained and controlled.

q: Uranium-238 or plutonium-238 are commonly used as fissionable nuclear fuel.
e: False. The right claim is this: Fissionable nuclear fuel is the material for fission reaction to take place, and uranium-235 or plutonium-239 can be used as fuel. Fission splits a heavy nucleus after a neutron bite, throwing fragments and more neutrons. The printed line wrongly says uranium-238 or plutonium-238 are commonly used as fissionable nuclear fuel.

q: Neutrons released from a fission reaction are slow neutrons and need to be sped up to maintain a chain reaction.
e: False. The right claim is this: Neutrons released from a fission reaction are fast neutrons and need to be slowed down to maintain a chain reaction. A neutron is uncharged; fission starts when a neutron is absorbed by a heavy nucleus. The printed line wrongly says neutrons released from a fission reaction are slow neutrons and need to be sped up to maintain a chain reaction.

q: Graphite and ordinary water as well as heavy water are used as moderators to slow down fast neutrons.
e: True. A neutron is uncharged; fission starts when a neutron is absorbed by a heavy nucleus. As heavy water are used as moderators to slow down fast neutrons.

q: Coolant is used to extract the heat produced by fission fragments when they slow down and stop in the reactor material.
e: True. A reactor is a vessel where a fission chain can be started, held, and steered. Fission fragments when they slow down and stop in the reactor material.

q: Boron and cadmium are used as control rods because they are excellent neutron emitting materials.
e: False. The right claim is this: Boron and cadmium are neutron absorbing materials used as control rods. A neutron is uncharged; fission starts when a neutron is absorbed by a heavy nucleus. The printed line wrongly says boron and cadmium are used as control rods because they are excellent neutron emitting materials.

q: The reactor vessel is a pressurized steel vessel that contains the reactor core, moderator, coolant and control rods.
e: True. A reactor is a vessel where a fission chain can be started, held, and steered. Steel vessel that contains the reactor core, moderator, coolant and control rods.

q: Shielding is a protective barrier that increases the passage of radiations from radioactive materials.
e: False. The right claim is this: Shielding is a protective barrier that reduces the passage of radiations from radioactive materials by absorbing them. Dense shielding soaks up radiation so the outside dose stays low. The printed line wrongly says shielding is a protective barrier that increases the passage of radiations from radioactive materials.

q: Materials which are radioactive and for which there is no further use are called radioactive waste.
e: True. Radioactive waste is leftover active material with no further use. And for which there is no further use are called radioactive waste.

q: Spent fuel are taken to a reprocessing plant where unused fuel and plutonium are removed, and the remaining waste is safe to release into the environment immediately.
e: False. Reprocessed leftover waste stays radioactive; it is not safe to dump at once. The printed line wrongly says spent fuel are taken to a reprocessing plant where unused fuel and plutonium are removed, and the remaining waste is safe to release into the environment immediately.

q: Strontium-90 becomes concentrated in bones and iodine-131 in the thyroid gland.
e: True. Strontium-90 becomes concentrated in bones and iodine-131 in the thyroid gland.

q: Plutonium is highly toxic and if breathed in, a very small amount can kill a person.
e: True. Plutonium is highly toxic and if breathed in, a very small amount can kill a person. And if breathed in, a very small amount can kill a person.

q: In an atomic bomb, a controlled chain reaction takes place so that a steady amount of energy is released over a long interval of time.
e: False. The right claim is this: In an atomic bomb, an uncontrolled chain reaction takes place so that an extremely large amount of energy is released in a short interval of time. A chain reaction is when fission neutrons go on to split further fuel nuclei. The printed line wrongly says in an atomic bomb, a controlled chain reaction takes place so that a steady amount of energy is released over a long interval of time.

q: When completely fissioned, 1 kg of uranium-235 releases the energy equivalently produced by 17 kilotons of trinitrotoluene (TNT).
e: True. When completely fissioned, 1 kg of uranium-235 releases the energy equivalently produced by 17 kilotons of trinitrotoluene (TNT). The value 1 kg is the figure this statement is using.

q: The detonation of an atomic bomb creates a characteristic mushroom-shaped cloud and produces a strong shock wave.
e: True. This detonation of an atomic bomb creates a characteristic mushroom-shaped cloud and produces a strong shock wave. Bomb creates a characteristic mushroom-shaped cloud and produces a strong shock wave.

q: The greenhouse gas emissions from nuclear fission power are much larger than those associated with coal, oil and gas.
e: False. The right claim is this: The greenhouse gas emissions from nuclear fission power are much smaller than those associated with coal, oil and gas. Fission splits a heavy nucleus after a neutron bite, throwing fragments and more neutrons. The printed line wrongly says the greenhouse gas emissions from nuclear fission power are much larger than those associated with coal, oil and gas.

q: The 1979 Three Mile Island accident and 1986 Chernobyl disaster ended the rapid growth of global nuclear power capacity.
e: True. This 1979 Three Mile Island accident and 1986 Chernobyl disaster ended the rapid growth of global nuclear power capacity. The year 1979 belongs to this fact, not a nearby discovery date.

q: A release of radioactive materials followed the 2011 Japanese tsunami which damaged the Fukushima I Nuclear Power Plant.
e: True. Radioactivity is nuclear: an unstable nucleus emits alpha, beta, or gamma. The year 2011 belongs to this fact, not a nearby discovery date.
